conventions.convention: The generic field is Q(A), with q=A⁴, q_K=A², q_L=A⁻² and ordinary Jones variable t=q⁻¹.
Colors have dimension N≥1. The positive crossing is P times the specified finite R series; the twist is (-1)^(N-1)A^(N²-1), and the pivotal diagonal has entries (-1)^(N-1)A^(2(N-1-2j)).

Normalize the generic framed trace by the inverse writhe power of the twist and by the generic quantum dimension. Root evaluation means substitution into the resulting integral Laurent polynomial, never division by the specialized quantum dimension.
The braid closure pairs bottom and top endpoints at the same position. In the downward-height diagrams the right input strand passes over the left at a positive generator.
The conjecture uses q_N=exp(2πi/N), eventual nonvanishing, and the real limit (2π/N)log|J_N(K;q_N)| for a smooth hyperbolic knot with a complete finite-volume metric and one peripheral torus cusp.
AC and Countable Choice accompany the invariant identification; finite fixed-braid matrix operations are distinguished from these categorical and isotopy assumptions.

load_bearing.statement: For every integer N≥1, the concrete module, finite R series, duality, pivotal comparison G_N, and twist λ_N in the normalized colored Jones definition are admissible ribbon data in the specified generated category with all module maps.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. For every N≥1 and finite braid word on b≥1 strands whose closure is a knot, the normalized generic quotient belongs to Z[A⁴,A⁻⁴]. Its unique representative in Z[q,q⁻¹] is braid-independent, equals 1 on the unknot, and agrees with Murakami’s explicit matrix convention in variable q; values at nonzero complex q are Laurent-polynomial evaluations.
For an N-dimensional color and a knot-closing braid β on n strands, J_N^gen(K;q)=λ_N^(-w(β)) Tr(G_N^⊗n ρ_N(β))/d_N. Define J_N(K;q) as its unique integral Laurent representative under q=A⁴.

alerts.finding: In alg-ribbon-evaluation-from-colored-braid-word, the Definition specifies the positive crossing c_{V_{a_i},V_{a_{i+1}}} and then says, “for a negative letter use its inverse.” For a current adjacent tuple (A,B), c_{A,B}^{-1} has source B⊗A, whereas the current source is A⊗B. Proof step 1.1 repeats that “the negative matrix is its typed inverse,” without reversing the ordered color pair. The required negative crossing has source A⊗B and is (c_{B,A})^{-1}, as explicitly specified for signed objects by thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor. Thus the general mixed-color procedure is ill-typed as written. The batch-89 invocation uses identical colors throughout, so this defect does not invalidate that invocation.

seams_checked.note: The open problem uses the supplied definition of a complete curvature-minus-one metric on the interior of the compact smooth knot exterior, finite volume and one peripheral torus cusp. It assumes such a metric and names its volume; it makes no additional existence or rigidity inference.

The consumer retains the generic field, absolute simplicity, scalar twist correction and choice hypotheses. Its N=2 matrices match the fundamental supplier, and the example uses the supplier’s extra loop factor and separate bracket/Jones identification correctly. The mixed-color inverse issue reported separately disappears for the constant color tuple used here.
